title: Resolving the Paradise name using the 1979 interview
summary: Schaap recalls that in 1979 Waters said the name came from Atlantic City; Waters accepts it is probable that the band took its name there before reaching New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Anything you could tell me about him?
No, I don't remember the name.
Uh huh.
Yeah.
Well, let me put it -
I think that, I think so, somethin' like that, I can't verify that so well. But I know one thing, that I knew that I was comin' to New York before I joined the band because they told me.

Let's try to tie up some loose ends on this transition from Boston to New York via Philadelphia and Atlantic City. First of all, in 1979 when we spoke at length about Charlie Johnson's Orchestra, we did a three hour interview -
Uh huh -
At that time -
That was in New York, yeah.
We were in New York.
Yeah. (PS laughs) Only, because we had, we were talkin' records. And we didn't make no records in Atlantic City.
That's right -
[ ], so that clears that out.
You're jumpin', you're answerin' the question before the question exists. I'm tryin' to give you a piece of information.
Yeah.
In April of 1979, you did a three hour interview with me about Charlie Johnson's Orchestra, and at that time you told me the name Paradise came from the Atlantic City Paradise.
I did?
Yeah.
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Well, OK, that's well correct then. Because -
OK, I'm not sayin' one is correct or the other, I just wanted to let you know that three years ago you used that -
If I have made a mistake about the first band that was there before, then they, it's easy, that Paradise name to get from in Atlantic City -
Well, it makes sense to use both, because it works both -
Yeah, yeah -

But what I'm tryin' to say is, I'm tryin' to get you to recognize the possibility, or at least tell me there is a possibility, that the band had not played in New York, in Small's Paradise, when you joined.

That's what I'm tryin' to think up now, that's what I'm recalling now, Phil. I'm, I just got to recall, I said I think that a band by the name of Snowden, Elmer Snowden was there and that there's another piano player I believe was there before Elmer Snowden or, you know, see. So in that case, we, it was, the band wasn't in New York -
And probably got its Paradise name in Atlantic City -
Yeah, yeah, at the Paradise Club, yeah.
